correctness.rationale: The crucial quantifiers were checked, including the empty simplex and cones. If K fails r-conicity, a subcomplex A on <=r vertices lies in no closed star; for every v some face sigma in A cannot be extended by v, so its vertex set is totally dominating. Conversely for a dominating S of size <=r, faces sigma_v witnessing each vertex generate a subcomplex A on <=r vertices contained in no star. Thus K r-conic iff gamma(K)>r, for all integers r>=-1. K is cone iff no totally dominating set exists, proving infinity case. For disjoint joins, a witness face alpha union beta for v in K fails join membership iff alpha union {v} fails in K, since beta is a valid L face; hence total domination holds exactly when both component sets totally dominate. Minimize cardinalities, covering cone/infinity cases. The provided verify.py correctly enumerates all 126 small nonempty labeled complexes and 144 joins, which corroborate but do not prove the general theorem.
residual_risks: The proof uses finite nonempty declared vertex sets and disjoint join vertices; no infinite locally finite generalization is asserted.
The open definition of subcomplex with empty simplex and r=-1 boundary is handled by equivalence.

originality.rationale: Aharoni–Berger (2006) states simplicial total domination via non-extendable faces; Barmak (2021) separately defines r-conicity through closed stars and proves only a lower join bound. The full texts checked provide the two ingredients separately, but not their identity or exact join additivity of maximal conicity; Farber appendix likewise restates conicity without the dual parameter. This is a short derivation once definitions are juxtaposed; novelty is bounded to the explicit cross-parameter formula and joins, not new connectivity bounds.
residual_risks: The duality is an elementary de Morgan equivalence; an unindexed later expository reference may explicitly state it under different notation.

An Aug-2026 Barmak–Farber paper on other combinatorial connectivity criteria was indexed but its full text was not accessible for substantive comparison; it is a possible uninspected later alias source.

value.rationale: This is an exact dictionary between independently used topology and combinatorial domination invariants. Its nontrivial mathematical purpose is to transfer conicity estimates to an existing total-domination parameter and upgrade Barmak's general one-sided join estimate to an equality for the maximal conicity index, including cones. Although the proof is short, the universal join structure and reusable equivalence are motivated, not an arbitrary renamed finite calculation.
residual_risks: The equivalence is elementary and yields no automatically new or sharper connectivity corollary compared with existing domination bounds; value is modest and structural.

final_claim: For every finite nonempty simplicial complex K, maximal conicity kappa(K)=tilde_gamma(K)-1 (infinity conventions); for finite nonempty K,L on disjoint vertex sets, simplicial total domination adds under joins and kappa(K*L)=kappa(K)+kappa(L)+1.
limitations: All finite nonempty K,L; no claim of new general connectivity sharpness or novel sphere example.
Barmak–Farber Aug2026 related primary full text not accessible; specific residual originality risk recorded.
